Presidential Gubernatorial Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group)
The Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX Group) has completed the purchase of a 10 per cent shareholding in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, East Africa’s largest stock exchange, to widen its reach in the region, where it already holds a similar equity interest in a bourse in Ethiopia.
The strategic stake supports its pan-African expansion ambition to grow its investment portfolio at scale as it continues to pursue regional leadership across West and East African markets, the company announced in a statement on Monday.
NGX Group said it sees the move as a key entry point into “one of East Africa’s most established capital markets,” helping enlarge its “investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and positioning the group to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s capital markets.”
“It also reflects NGX Group’s disciplined approach to capital allocation, balancing strategic growth opportunities with its commitment to sustainable shareholder returns,” it added.
The group established its footprint in the region in April 2024 when it acquired a stake in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange without disclosing the size of the acquisition.
At the time, the Government of Ethiopia held 25 per cent in the bourse, with the remaining 75 per cent variously owned by private sector players.
“Through these investments, NGX Group continues to pursue opportunities that enhance its regional participation, diversify its sources of investment returns and support the development of more connected and competitive African capital markets,” NGX Group CEO Temi Popoola said.

Taking an equity position in security exchanges in Kenya and Ethiopia mirrors the group’s drive to take its partnership with other exchanges on the continent beyond cross-border market collaborations. The broader push involves harnessing the value and investment prospects that African economies hold through their capital market operations.
NGX Group is optimistic that its investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange will advance its objectives of stronger regional integration, portfolio diversification and shareholder value.
“African capital markets are at an inflexion point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture,” Umaru Kwairanga, chair of NGX Group, said.
“Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent,” he added.
